---
title: "Autoregressive Model"
description: "A model that predicts each value or token conditioned on preceding values."
term: "Autoregressive Model"
letter: "A"
category: "Generative AI"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

An autoregressive model generates or predicts a sequence one element at a
time. Each new prediction uses the preceding elements as context.

## Technical explanation

For a sequence $x_1,\ldots,x_T$, an autoregressive model factorizes the
joint distribution as
$$
p(x_1,\ldots,x_T)=\prod_{t=1}^{T}p(x_t\mid x_1,\ldots,x_{t-1}) 
$$
In a language model, the elements are usually tokens. Training commonly
uses next-token prediction, while generation repeatedly samples or selects
a next token conditioned on the prefix.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Many language and generative models use autoregressive generation.
Understanding the sequential process helps engineers reason about latency,
context limits, decoding strategies, and why generated output can diverge
from an intended answer.

## How it works

The model receives a prefix and predicts a probability distribution over
the next token. A decoding rule chooses a token, appends it to the prefix,
and repeats until a stop condition is reached. The rule may select the
highest-probability token or sample from a modified distribution.

## Practical example

Given the prompt "The capital of France is", an autoregressive language
model predicts a distribution for the next token, emits a token, and then
uses the extended text to predict subsequent tokens.

## Common misconceptions

- Autoregressive describes a factorization or generation pattern, not a
  guarantee of factual correctness.
- The most probable next token at each step does not always produce the
  most desirable complete response.
- Autoregressive generation is sequential across generated positions even
  when the model uses parallel computation during training.
